record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: When max smti instances have master lists on one or both sides, determine whether those structural restrictions permit improved approximation algorithms and better upper bounds than are currently known.

evidence.quote: it is an open question as to whether improved upper bounds exist in the presence of master lists on one or both sides.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An instance of the Stable Marriage problem with Ties and Incomplete lists (SMTI) consists of two disjoint finite sets, a set of men M and a set of women W. Each person p has a preference list that is a strict ranking of a subset of the opposite sex except that ties (groups of equally-preferred partners) are permitted; person q is acceptable to p iff q appears in p's list, and acceptability is symmetric. A matching is a set of disjoint acceptable man–woman pairs. A matching is stable if there is no blocking pair, i.e., no acceptable pair (m,w) outside the matching such that each of m and w is either unmatched or strictly prefers the other to their current partner. MAX-SMTI is the optimization problem of finding a stable matching of maximum cardinality; it is NP-hard and APX-hard in general, with current best approximation ratio 3/2.

Say that an SMTI instance has a master list on the men's side if there is a single preference ranking (possibly with ties) over all women such that each man's preference list is the restriction of this master ranking to the women acceptable to him; symmetrically for a master list on the women's side. An instance has master lists on both sides if both restrictions hold.

Problem: For MAX-SMTI restricted to instances having a master list on one side, and separately for MAX-SMTI restricted to instances having master lists on both sides, determine the best possible polynomial-time approximation ratio. In particular, exhibit approximation algorithms with ratio strictly below 3/2 (the current best for general MAX-SMTI), or prove improved inapproximability upper bounds that exploit the master-list structure.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that for general MAX-SMTI the best polynomial-time approximation ratio remains 3/2, and improvements for the master-list restricted variants are not reported in the literature surveyed. No paper was found that resolves the question of whether master lists on one or both sides admit better approximation ratios, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Tight Approximation Bound for the Stable Marriage problem with restricted ties
status_evidence.snippet: Current best approximation ratio for MAX-SMTI is 3/2; improved bounds known for restricted variants such as one-sided ties, but master-list restrictions not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: State of the art for MAX-SMTI approximation is 3/2 with no improvement specific to master lists reported.

status_evidence.title: Hardness and Approximation Results for Some Variants of Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys hardness/approximation results for SMTI variants; master-list one/both-sided improvement remains unaddressed.
status_evidence.claim: No improved approximation specifically for master-list-restricted MAX-SMTI is reported in recent surveys.
